title: Two Sum
statement:
Given an array of integers `nums` and an integer `target`, return the indices of the
two numbers such that they add up to `target`.

You may assume that each input has exactly one solution, and you may not use
the same element twice. The answer may be returned in any order.

Because the answer is the pair itself, not the sum, order does not matter.
reference_solution: vector<int> twoSum(vector<int>& nums, int target){unordered_map<int,int> seen; for(int i=0;i<(int)nums.size();++i){auto it=seen.find(target-nums[i]); if(it!=seen.end()) return {it->second,i};seen[nums[i]]=i;} return {};}

title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
statement:
You are given an array `prices` where `prices[i]` is the price of a given stock on day `i`.

Return the maximum profit you can achieve from buying once and selling once,
later. If you cannot achieve profit, return `0`.

You must buy before you sell, and the answer is the price at the sell minus the
price at the buy.
reference_solution: int maxProfit(vector<int>& prices){int lo=INT_MAX,best=0;for(int p:prices){lo=min(lo,p);best=max(best,p-lo);}return best;}

title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock II
statement:
You are given an array `prices` where `prices[i]` is the price of a given stock on day `i`.

Return the maximum profit you can achieve. You may buy and sell as many times
as you like, but you may only hold one share at a time.

You can think of this as collecting every upward step in the price, because a
rise broken into smaller rises earns exactly as much as the same rise taken in
one go.
reference_solution: int maxProfit(vector<int>& prices){int best=0;for(int i=1;i<(int)prices.size();++i) best+=max(0,prices[i]-prices[i-1]);return best;}

title: Contains Duplicate
statement:
Given an integer array `nums`, return `true` if any value appears at least twice,
and `false` if every element is distinct.
reference_solution: bool containsDuplicate(vector<int>& nums){unordered_set<int> s;for(int x:nums) if(!s.insert(x).second) return true; return false;}

title: Valid Parentheses
statement:
Given a string `s` containing only the characters `(`, `)`, `{`, `}`, `[` and `]`,
return `true` if every opening bracket is closed by the same type of bracket in
the correct order, and `false` otherwise.
reference_solution: bool isValid(string s){vector<char> st; for(char c:s){if(c=='('||c=='['||c=='{') st.push_back(c); else if(st.empty()) return false;else if((c==')'&&st.back()!='(')||(c==']'&&st.back()!='[')||(c=='}'&&st.back()!='{'))return false; else st.pop_back();} return st.empty();}

title: Valid Palindrome
statement:
Given a string `s`, return `true` if it is a palindrome, ignoring case and
non-alphanumeric characters.

A palindrome reads the same forwards and backwards, so compare the string from
both ends, skipping anything that is not a letter or a digit.

examples.input: s = "A man, a plan, a canal: Panama"

constraints: s consists of letters, digits, spaces and punctuation.
reference_solution: bool isPalindrome(string s){int i=0,j=(int)s.size()-1;while(i<j){while(i<j&&!isalnum((unsigned char)s[i]))++i;while(i<j&&!isalnum((unsigned char)s[j]))--j;if(tolower((unsigned char)s[i])!=tolower((unsigned char)s[j])) return false;++i;--j;}return true;}

title: Maximum Subarray
statement:
Given an integer array `nums`, return the largest sum of a contiguous non-empty
subarray.

A subarray is a contiguous slice of the array. The answer is always at least
`nums[0]`, because a single element is itself a valid subarray.
reference_solution: int maxSubArray(vector<int>& nums){int best=nums[0],cur=nums[0];for(int i=1;i<(int)nums.size();++i){cur=max(nums[i],cur+nums[i]);best=max(best,cur);}return best;}

title: Missing Number
statement:
Given an array `nums` of `n` unique integers from `0` to `n-1`, return the one
number missing from the range.

Sum the array and compare against the arithmetic series `n * (n + 1) / 2` — the
difference is the missing number, and it needs no extra space.
reference_solution: int missingNumber(vector<int>& nums){long long n=nums.size();long long expected=n*(n+1)/2,actual=0; for(int x:nums) actual+=x;return (int)(expected-actual);}

title: Single Number
statement:
Given an integer array `nums` where every element appears exactly twice except
for one element that appears exactly once, return that element.

XOR cancels a number XORed with itself, so XORing everything together leaves
the odd one out.
constraints: Exactly one element appears once; the rest appear twice.
reference_solution: int singleNumber(vector<int>& nums){int r=0; for(int x:nums) r^=x; return r;}

title: Climb Stairs
statement:
You are climbing a staircase with `n` steps. You can either climb one or two
steps at a time. Return the number of distinct ways to reach the top.

The answer follows the Fibonacci sequence: ways(1) = 1, ways(2) = 2, and each
later step is the sum of the two before it.
reference_solution: int climbStairs(int n){int a=1,b=1; for(int i=2;i<=n;++i){int t=a+b;a=b;b=t;} return b;}

title: Plus One
statement:
You are given a non-negative integer represented as an array of its digits,
stored in most-significant-first order. Return the result of adding one to it.

The digits may be very long, so do not convert the whole thing to an integer.
Carry from the right and only grow the array if the carry runs off the end.
constraints: The array does not contain leading zeros.
reference_solution: vector<int> plusOne(vector<int>& digits){int i=(int)digits.size()-1;while(i>=0&&digits[i]==9){digits[i]=0;--i;} if(i>=0) ++digits[i];else digits.insert(digits.begin(),1); return digits;}

title: Move Zeroes
statement:
Given an integer array `nums`, move all the `0`s to the end of it, keeping the
relative order of the non-zero elements.

Return the array in place.
reference_solution: void moveZeroes(vector<int>& nums){int w=0; for(int i=0;i<(int)nums.size();++i)if(nums[i]!=0) nums[w++]=nums[i]; while(w<(int)nums.size()) nums[w++]=0;}

title: Valid Anagram
statement:
Given two strings `s` and `t`, return `true` if `t` is an anagram of `s`.

An anagram uses exactly the same letters with exactly the same counts, in any
order.
constraints: s and t consist of lowercase letters.
reference_solution: bool isAnagram(string s, string t){if(s.size()!=t.size()) return false;int freq[26]={0}; for(char c:s) ++freq[c-'a']; for(char c:t) --freq[c-'a'];for(int i=0;i<26;++i) if(freq[i]) return false; return true;}

title: Roman to Integer
statement:
Given a roman numeral, convert it to an integer.

Roman numerals are built from seven symbols. `I` is 1, `V` is 5, `X` is 10,
`L` is 50, `C` is 100, `D` is 500 and `M` is 1000. A symbol before a larger one
is subtracted; otherwise it is added.
constraints: s is a valid roman numeral.
reference_solution: int romanToInt(string s){unordered_map<char,int> v={{'I',1},{'V',5},{'X',10},{'L',50},{'C',100},{'D',500},{'M',1000}}; int r=0; for(int i=0;i<(int)s.size();++i){int cur=v[s[i]]; int nxt=(i+1<(int)s.size())?v[s[i+1]]:0; r+= cur<nxt? -cur:cur;}return r;}

title: Reverse Integer
statement:
Given a signed 32-bit integer `x`, return `x` with its digits reversed.

If reversing `x` makes the value fall outside the signed 32-bit range
`[-2^31, 2^31 - 1]`, return `0` instead.
reference_solution: int reverse(int x){long long r=0; while(x){r=r*10+x%10;x/=10;}if(r<-2147483648LL||r>2147483647LL) return 0; return (int)r;}

title: Majority Element
statement:
Given an array `nums` of size `n`, return the majority element — the element
that appears more than `n / 2` times.

You may assume the majority element always exists in the array.
constraints: The majority element is guaranteed to exist.
reference_solution: int majorityElement(vector<int>& nums){unordered_map<int,int> c;for(int x:nums) if(++c[x]>(int)nums.size()/2) return x; return 0;}

title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
statement:
Return the length of the longest substring of `s` that contains no repeated
characters.

Slide a window over the string, remembering where each character was last seen,
and move the left edge past the previous occurrence when a repeat appears.
constraints: s consists of English letters, digits, spaces and punctuation.
reference_solution: int lengthOfLongestSubstring(string s){unordered_map<char,int> last; int best=0,l=0;for(int i=0;i<(int)s.size();++i){auto it=last.find(s[i]); if(it!=last.end()) l=max(l,it->second+1);last[s[i]]=i; best=max(best,i-l+1);} return best;}

title: First Missing Positive
statement:
Given an unsorted integer array `nums`, return the smallest missing positive
integer.

The answer is always between `1` and `n + 1` where `n` is the length. Ignore
anything zero or negative, and anything larger than `n`.
reference_solution: int firstMissingPositive(vector<int>& nums){int n=nums.size(); vector<bool> seen(n+1,false);for(int x:nums) if(x>0&&x<=n) seen[x]=true;for(int i=1;i<=n;++i) if(!seen[i]) return i; return n+1;}

title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
statement:
Given an ascending array of distinct integers `nums` that has been rotated at
an unknown pivot, return the index of `target`, or `-1` if it is not present.

Binary search still works: one half of the range is always sorted, so decide
which half to keep using the target value.
constraints: All values in nums are distinct.
nums is a rotation of a sorted array.
reference_solution: int search(vector<int>& nums, int target){int l=0,r=(int)nums.size()-1;while(l<=r){int m=l+(r-l)/2; if(nums[m]==target) return m;if(nums[l]<=nums[m]){if(nums[l]<=target&&target<nums[m]) r=m-1; else l=m+1;}else {if(nums[m]<target&&target<=nums[r]) l=m+1; else r=m-1;}} return -1;}

title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array
statement:
Given a sorted array `nums`, remove the duplicates in place so that each
distinct value appears only once, and return the number of distinct values `k`.

The first `k` elements of `nums` should be the sorted unique values.
constraints: nums is sorted in non-decreasing order.
reference_solution: int removeDuplicates(vector<int>& nums){if(nums.empty()) return 0; int k=1;for(int i=1;i<(int)nums.size();++i) if(nums[i]!=nums[k-1]) nums[k++]=nums[i]; return k;}

title: Squares of a Sorted Array
statement:
Given an integer array `nums` sorted in ascending order, return an array of the
squares of each number, also in ascending order.

Square the largest remaining value from either end, which keeps the result
sorted without sorting it afterwards.
constraints: nums is sorted in ascending order.
reference_solution: vector<int> sortedSquares(vector<int>& nums){int n=nums.size(); vector<int> out(n);int l=0,r=n-1; for(int i=n-1;i>=0;--i){int a=nums[l]*nums[l],b=nums[r]*nums[r];if(a>b){out[i]=a;++l;} else {out[i]=b;--r;}} return out;}

title: Intersection of Two Arrays
statement:
Given two integer arrays `nums1` and `nums2`, return their intersection —
the distinct values that appear in both arrays.

The answer may be returned in any order.
reference_solution: vector<int> intersection(vector<int>& nums1, vector<int>& nums2){unordered_set<int> a(nums1.begin(),nums1.end()); vector<int> out; unordered_set<int> added;for(int x:nums2) if(a.count(x) && added.insert(x).second) out.push_back(x);sort(out.begin(),out.end()); return out;}

title: Sort Colors
statement:
Given an array `nums` containing `n` integers, where each integer is `0`, `1`
or `2`, sort it so that all the `0`s come first, then all the `1`s, then all the
`2`s.

Return the array in place.
reference_solution: void sortColors(vector<int>& nums){int lo=0,mid=0,hi=(int)nums.size()-1;while(mid<=hi){ if(nums[mid]==0) swap(nums[lo++],nums[mid++]); else if(nums[mid]==2) swap(nums[mid],nums[hi--]); else ++mid;}}

title: Steps to Reduce a Number to Zero
statement:
Given a non-negative integer `n`, return the number of steps to reduce it to
zero. In one step you may either subtract one, or divide by an even number.

Subtracting one is always available, so the answer is always finite.
reference_solution: int stepNumber(int n){int steps=0; while(n>0){ if(n%2==0) n/=2; else n-=1; ++steps;} return steps;}

title: Reverse Words in a String
statement:
Return the string with its words in reverse order.

Trim leading and trailing spaces, and collapse runs of spaces into a single
space between words.
constraints: s contains letters and spaces only.
reference_solution: string reverseWords(string s){vector<string> w; string cur; for(char c:s){if(c==' '){ if(!cur.empty()){w.push_back(cur);cur.clear();} } else cur+=c;}if(!cur.empty()) w.push_back(cur); string out; for(int i=(int)w.size()-1;i>=0;--i){if(!out.empty()) out+=' '; out+=w[i];} return out;}

title: 3Sum
statement:
Given an integer array `nums`, return all the unique triples
`[nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]]` such that `i`, `j` and `k` are distinct and the
three numbers sum to zero.

The solution set must not contain duplicate triples, and the order of each
triple, and of the list of triples, does not matter.
reference_solution: vector<vector<int>> threeSum(vector<int>& nums){sort(nums.begin(),nums.end());vector<vector<int>> out; int n=nums.size();for(int i=0;i+2<n;++i){ if(i>0&&nums[i]==nums[i-1]) continue; int l=i+1,r=n-1;while(l<r){long long s=(long long)nums[i]+nums[l]+nums[r];if(s==0){out.push_back({nums[i],nums[l],nums[r]}); ++l; --r;while(l<r&&nums[l]==nums[l-1])++l; while(l<r&&nums[r]==nums[r+1])--r;}else if(s<0)++l; else --r;}} return out;}

title: Container With Most Water
statement:
Given `height` where each element is the height of a vertical line, return
the largest possible area of water a container can hold.

The container is formed by two lines, and the area is the smaller height times
the distance between them.
reference_solution: int maxArea(vector<int>& height){int l=0,r=(int)height.size()-1,best=0;while(l<r){int a=min(height[l],height[r])*(r-l); best=max(best,a);if(height[l]<height[r]) ++l; else --r;} return best;}

title: Group Anagrams
statement:
Given an array of strings `strs`, group the anagrams together and return the
groups. The order of the groups and of the strings within a group does not
matter.

Two strings are anagrams when their sorted characters are equal.
constraints: strs[i] consists of lowercase English letters.
reference_solution: vector<vector<string>> groupAnagrams(vector<string>& strs){unordered_map<string,vector<string>> g; for(auto&w:strs){string k=w; sort(k.begin(),k.end());g[k].push_back(w);} vector<vector<string>> out; for(auto&kv:g){sort(kv.second.begin(),kv.second.end());out.push_back(kv.second);} sort(out.begin(),out.end()); return out;}

title: Product of Array Except Self
statement:
Given an integer array `nums`, return an array `answer` where `answer[i]` is
the product of all the elements of `nums` except `nums[i]`.

You must solve it in `O(n)` time and without using a division operation.
constraints: The product of any prefix or suffix fits in a 64-bit integer.
reference_solution: vector<int> productExceptSelf(vector<int>& nums){int n=nums.size(); vector<int> out(n,1);int pre=1; for(int i=0;i<n;++i){out[i]=pre; pre*=nums[i];}int suf=1; for(int i=n-1;i>=0;--i){out[i]*=suf; suf*=nums[i];} return out;}

title: Daily Temperatures
statement:
Given an array `temps` of daily temperatures, return an array `answer` where
`answer[i]` is the number of days you have to wait for a warmer temperature.

If there is no future day that is warmer, the answer is `0`.
reference_solution: vector<int> dailyTemperatures(vector<int>& temps){int n=temps.size(); vector<int> out(n,0);vector<int> st; for(int i=0;i<n;++i){while(!st.empty()&&temps[st.back()]<temps[i]){out[st.back()]=i-st.back(); st.pop_back();} st.push_back(i);} return out;}

title: House Robber
statement:
You are given an array `nums` of non-negative integers representing the amount
of money in each house. Return the most money you can rob without ever robbing
two adjacent houses.

Take the maximum of robbing the current house and skipping it.
reference_solution: int rob(vector<int>& nums){int a=0,b=0; for(int x:nums){int t=max(b,a+x); a=b; b=t;} return b;}

title: Coin Change
statement:
Given an integer array `coins` of distinct denominations and an integer
`amount`, return the fewest number of coins needed to make up `amount`.

If it cannot be made, return `-1`. You have an unlimited number of each coin.
reference_solution: int coinChange(vector<int>& coins,int amount){vector<int> dp(amount+1,amount+1); dp[0]=0;for(int a=1;a<=amount;++a) for(int c:coins) if(c<=a) dp[a]=min(dp[a],dp[a-c]+1);return dp[amount]>amount?-1:dp[amount];}

title: Word Break
statement:
Given a string `s` and a dictionary `wordDict`, return `true` if `s` can be
segmented into a sequence of one or more dictionary words.

A word in the dictionary can be reused as many times as you like.
reference_solution: bool wordBreak(string s, vector<string>& wordDict){unordered_set<string> d(wordDict.begin(),wordDict.end());int n=s.size(); vector<bool> ok(n+1,false); ok[0]=true;for(int i=1;i<=n;++i) for(int j=0;j<i;++j) if(ok[j]&&d.count(s.substr(j,i-j))){ok[i]=true;break;}return ok[n];}

title: Combination Sum
statement:
Given an array of distinct integers `candidates` and a target `target`,
return all possible combinations in `candidates` where the chosen numbers sum
to `target`.

Each candidate may be chosen unlimited times, and the same candidate may not
appear more than once in a combination.
constraints: All elements of candidates are distinct.
reference_solution: vector<vector<int>> combinationSum(vector<int>& candidates,int target){vector<vector<int>> out; vector<int> cur; sort(candidates.begin(),candidates.end());function<void(int,int)> go=[&](int start,int rem){ if(rem==0){out.push_back(cur);return;}for(int i=start;i<(int)candidates.size();++i){ if(candidates[i]>rem) break;cur.push_back(candidates[i]); go(i,rem-candidates[i]); cur.pop_back();}}; go(0,target); return out;}

title: Subsets
statement:
Given an integer array `nums` of unique elements, return all possible
subsets (the power set).

The solution must not contain duplicate subsets, and the order of the subsets
and of the elements within them does not matter.
constraints: All elements of nums are unique.
reference_solution: vector<vector<int>> subsets(vector<int>& nums){vector<vector<int>> out; vector<int> cur;function<void(int)> go=[&](int start){ out.push_back(cur); for(int i=start;i<(int)nums.size();++i){cur.push_back(nums[i]); go(i+1); cur.pop_back();}}; go(0); return out;}

title: Number of Islands
statement:
Given an `m x n` binary grid where `1` is land and `0` is water, return the
number of islands.

An island is a group of land cells connected up, down, left and right. Flood
fill each island as you find it.
reference_solution: int numIslands(vector<vector<int>>& grid){int m=grid.size(); if(!m) return 0; int n=grid[0].size(),count=0; function<void(int,int)> go=[&](int r,int c){ if(r<0||r>=m||c<0||c>=n||!grid[r][c]) return;grid[r][c]=0; go(r+1,c); go(r-1,c); go(r,c+1); go(r,c-1);};for(int i=0;i<m;++i) for(int j=0;j<n;++j) if(grid[i][j]){++count; go(i,j);} return count;}

title: Course Schedule
statement:
There are `n` courses, numbered 0 to `n-1`, and a prerequisite array
`prereq` where `prereq[i]` lists the courses that must be taken before course `i`.

Return `true` if you can finish all the courses, and `false` if there is a
cycle. A cycle means no ordering of the courses works.
constraints: prereq[i] contains distinct integers in [0, n).
reference_solution: bool canFinish(int n, vector<vector<int>>& prereq){vector<int> indeg(n,0);for(auto&v:prereq) for(int c:v) ++indeg[c]; queue<int> q; for(int i=0;i<n;++i) if(!indeg[i]) q.push(i);int done=0; while(!q.empty()){int u=q.front();q.pop();++done; for(int v:prereq[u]) if(--indeg[v]==0) q.push(v);}return done==n;}

title: Set Matrix Zeroes
statement:
Given an `m x n` matrix, if an element is `0` set its entire row and column to
zero. Return the result in place.

Use the first row and first column to remember which rows and columns need
zeroing, so no extra memory is needed.
reference_solution: void setZeroes(vector<vector<int>>& matrix){int m=matrix.size(); if(!m) return; int n=matrix[0].size();bool row=false,col=false; for(int j=0;j<n;++j) if(matrix[0][j]==0) row=true;for(int i=0;i<m;++i) if(matrix[i][0]==0) col=true;for(int i=1;i<m;++i) for(int j=1;j<n;++j) if(matrix[i][j]==0){matrix[i][0]=0; matrix[0][j]=0;}for(int i=1;i<m;++i) for(int j=1;j<n;++j) if(matrix[i][0]==0||matrix[0][j]==0) matrix[i][j]=0;if(col) for(int i=0;i<m;++i) matrix[i][0]=0; if(row) for(int j=0;j<n;++j) matrix[0][j]=0;}

title: Spiral Matrix
statement:
Given an `m x n` matrix, return all its elements in spiral order — clockwise,
starting at the top-left corner.

Shrink the boundaries after each pass until they cross.
reference_solution: vector<int> spiralOrder(vector<vector<int>>& matrix){vector<int> out; if(matrix.empty()) return out;int m=matrix.size(), n=matrix[0].size(), top=0,bot=m-1,left=0,right=n-1;while(top<=bot&&left<=right){ for(int j=left;j<=right;++j) out.push_back(matrix[top][j]); ++top;for(int i=top;i<=bot;++i) out.push_back(matrix[i][right]); --right;if(top<=bot){ for(int j=right;j>=left;--j) out.push_back(matrix[bot][j]); --bot;}if(left<=right){ for(int i=bot;i>=top;--i) out.push_back(matrix[i][left]); ++left;}}return out;}

title: Rotate Image
statement:
You are given an `n x n` 2D matrix representing an image. Rotate the image
by 90 degrees clockwise, in place.

Transposing then reversing each row gives the same result as rotating 90
degrees clockwise.
reference_solution: void rotate(vector<vector<int>>& matrix){int n=matrix.size();for(int i=0;i<n;++i) for(int j=i+1;j<n;++j) swap(matrix[i][j],matrix[j][i]);for(int i=0;i<n;++i) reverse(matrix[i].begin(),matrix[i].end());}

title: Search a 2D Matrix
statement:
Given an `m x n` matrix where every row is sorted ascending and the first
integer of a row is strictly greater than the last integer of the row before
it, return `true` if `target` is in the matrix.

Treat the matrix as one sorted array and binary search it.
constraints: Each row is sorted in ascending order.
The first integer of a row is greater than the last integer of the row before it.
reference_solution: bool searchMatrix(vector<vector<int>>& matrix,int target){if(matrix.empty()||matrix[0].empty()) return false;int m=matrix.size(), n=matrix[0].size(), l=0,r=m*n-1;while(l<=r){int mid=l+(r-l)/2, val=matrix[mid/n][mid%n];if(val==target) return true; if(val<target) l=mid+1; else r=mid-1;} return false;}

title: Unique Paths
statement:
There is a grid of `m x n` cells. A robot starts at the top-left corner and
can only move right or down, and must reach the bottom-right corner.

Return the number of possible paths.
reference_solution: int uniquePaths(int m, int n){vector<int> row(n,1); for(int i=1;i<m;++i) for(int j=1;j<n;++j)row[j]+=row[j-1]; return row[n-1];}

title: Jump Game
statement:
You are given an integer array `nums` where `nums[i]` is the maximum jump
length from index `i`. Return `true` if you can reach the last index.

Keep track of the furthest index reachable so far.
reference_solution: bool canJump(vector<int>& nums){int far=0; for(int i=0;i<(int)nums.size();++i){if(i>far) return false; far=max(far,i+nums[i]);} return true;}

title: Decode Ways
statement:
A message containing letters `A` to `Z` is being encoded as numbers `1` to `26`.
`1` decodes to `A`, `2` to `B`, and so on, so `12` decodes to `L`.

Given the encoded string, return the number of ways to decode it. Return `0` if
the string cannot be decoded.
reference_solution: int numDecodings(string s){int n=s.size(); if(n==0) return 0; vector<int> dp(n+1,0); dp[0]=1;for(int i=1;i<=n;++i){ if(s[i-1]!='0') dp[i]+=dp[i-1];if(i>=2 && s[i-2]=='1') dp[i]+=dp[i-2];else if(i>=2 && s[i-2]=='2' && s[i-1]<='6') dp[i]+=dp[i-2];} return dp[n];}

title: Majority Element II
statement:
Given an integer array `nums`, return all the elements that appear more than
`n / 3` times.

You may return the answer in any order, and the answer is at most two
elements long.
reference_solution: vector<int> majorityElementTwo(vector<int>& nums){unordered_map<int,int> c; for(int x:nums) ++c[x];vector<int> out; for(auto&kv:c) if(kv.second>(int)nums.size()/3) out.push_back(kv.first);sort(out.begin(),out.end()); return out;}

title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
statement:
Given two sorted arrays `nums1` and `nums2` of size `m` and `n`, return the
median of the two sorted arrays combined.

You may not concatenate the arrays; the solution must run in `O(log(m + n))`
time.
constraints: Both arrays are sorted in non-decreasing order.
reference_solution: double findMedianSortedArrays(vector<int>& nums1, vector<int>& nums2){if(nums1.size()>nums2.size()) return findMedianSortedArrays(nums2,nums1);int m=nums1.size(),n=nums2.size(),lo=0,hi=m; while(lo<=hi){int i=(lo+hi)/2,j=(m+n+1)/2-i;int l1=(i==0)?INT_MIN:nums1[i-1], r1=(i==m)?INT_MAX:nums1[i];int l2=(j==0)?INT_MIN:nums2[j-1], r2=(j==n)?INT_MAX:nums2[j];if(l1<=r2&&l2<=r1){ if((m+n)%2) return (double)max(l1,l2); return ((double)max(l1,l2)+min(r1,r2))/2.0;}else if(l1>r2) hi=i-1; else lo=i+1;} return 0.0;}

title: Longest Palindromic Substring
statement:
Given a string `s`, return the longest palindromic substring of `s`.

A palindrome reads the same forwards and backwards.
constraints: s consists of digits and English letters.
reference_solution: string longestPalindrome(string s){int n=s.size(); if(n==0) return ""; string best(1,s[0]);auto expand=[&](int l,int r){while(l>=0&&r<n&&s[l]==s[r]){--l;++r;} int len=r-l-1;if(len>(int)best.size()) best=s.substr(l+1,len);};for(int i=0;i<n;++i){expand(i,i); expand(i,i+1);} return best;}

title: Trapping Rain Water
statement:
Given `height` where each element is the height of a vertical bar, return how
much water it can trap after raining.

The water at an index is bounded by the tallest bar to its left and the tallest
bar to its right, minus its own height.
reference_solution: int trap(vector<int>& height){int n=height.size(); if(n<3) return 0;int l=0,r=n-1,leftMax=0,rightMax=0,water=0;while(l<r){ if(height[l]<height[r]){ leftMax=max(leftMax,height[l]); water+=leftMax-height[l]; ++l;}else { rightMax=max(rightMax,height[r]); water+=rightMax-height[r]; --r;}} return water;}

title: Subarray Sum Equals K
statement:
Given an array `nums` of integers and an integer `k`, return the total number of
continuous subarrays whose sum equals `k`.

Track how many times each prefix sum has been seen.
reference_solution: int subarraySum(vector<int>& nums,int k){unordered_map<int,int> seen; seen[0]=1; int sum=0,count=0;for(int x:nums){sum+=x; auto it=seen.find(sum-k); if(it!=seen.end()) count+=it->second; ++seen[sum];}return count;}

title: Word Search
statement:
Given an `m x n` board of characters and a word `word`, return `true` if `word`
exists in the board.

The word must be formed from letters of sequentially adjacent cells, moving
up, down, left or right. The same cell may not be used twice.
constraints: board[i][j] is an uppercase English letter.
word consists of uppercase English letters.
reference_solution: bool exist(vector<vector<char>>& board,string word){int m=board.size(); if(!m) return false; int n=board[0].size();function<bool(int,int,int)> go=[&](int r,int c,int k){ if(r<0||r>=m||c<0||c>=n) return false;if(board[r][c]!=word[k]) return false; if(k+1==(int)word.size()) return true;char save=board[r][c]; board[r][c]='#'; bool ok=go(r+1,c,k+1)||go(r-1,c,k+1)||go(r,c+1,k+1)||go(r,c-1,k+1);board[r][c]=save; return ok; };for(int i=0;i<m;++i) for(int j=0;j<n;++j) if(go(i,j,0)) return true; return false;}
